A speech frame is a short segment of audio treated as approximately stable for acoustic analysis. Speech recognizers commonly analyze overlapping intervals on the order of about ten milliseconds.

Each frame is transformed by [[Speech Feature Extraction]] into measurements such as filter-bank energies. A sequence of frames lets an [[Acoustic Model]] track how speech evolves over time.

A speech recognition grammar specifies the words and phrase patterns a recognizer should consider in a constrained interaction. Restricting the search space can improve accuracy when the next valid responses are predictable.

A [[Directed Prompt]] can establish such expectations for the user and system. Broad assistants need more open statistical models because their possible utterances cannot be enumerated compactly.

A speech synthesizer generates the acoustic waveform for a planned sequence of speech sounds and prosodic targets. It may concatenate recorded units, predict acoustic parameters, or generate audio directly with a neural model.

The synthesizer is the final computational stage of [[Text-to-Speech]] before digital-to-analog conversion and playback. Its output quality depends on the linguistic and prosodic information supplied upstream.

A speech-to-text service exposes [[Automatic Speech Recognition]] through a network interface. A device sends captured audio to a remote system and receives a transcript that another assistant component can interpret.

Centralized services can use large models and compute resources, but they introduce latency, connectivity, and privacy concerns. Local [[Wake Word]] detection can limit transmission to audio that follows a likely activation.

A sphere with center $(h,k,l)$ and radius $r$ is the set of points satisfying

$$(x-h)^2+(y-k)^2+(z-l)^2=r^2.$$

The equation fixes the three-dimensional distance from every surface point to the center, extending the planar [[Circle Equation]] by one coordinate.

A sphere-AABB intersection test finds the point on an axis-aligned box closest to the sphere center by clamping each coordinate to the box interval. The sphere intersects when the squared distance to that closest point is no greater than the squared radius.

This reduces a mixed-shape test to [[Point-in-AABB Test|clamping]] plus a distance comparison. It also supplies a useful closest point for later response calculations.

A spherical triangle is a region on a sphere bounded by three arcs of [[Great Circle]]s. Its side lengths are measured as central angles, and its vertex angles are angles between the corresponding great-circle planes. Unlike a Euclidean triangle, its interior-angle sum is greater than $180^\circ$.

A spike is a timeboxed backlog item whose primary result is knowledge. A team uses it to research, experiment, or prototype when uncertainty prevents responsible estimation or design.

The spike answers a stated question and ends at its time limit. Any production feature revealed by the work is planned separately, preventing investigation from silently becoming unbounded implementation.

A spiking neuron maintains an internal activation potential that changes as input pulses arrive and decays when they do not. It emits an output event only when the potential crosses a threshold. Timing therefore matters: enough inputs must occur within a suitable window to trigger a spike.

Kelleher contrasts this event-driven unit with a standard artificial neuron that computes an activation from the inputs at each processing step. In [[Neuromorphic Computing]], sparse firing can reduce repeated activity and energy use. It is a hardware-oriented computational model inspired by biological signaling, not a claim that all neural-network tasks are better expressed with spikes.

A spiral model combines elements of both waterfall and iterative approaches. Like the waterfall model, a spiral development model delineates a clear series of steps. But it also breaks down the process into a series of loops or “phases” that give development teams more flexibility to analyze, test and modify software throughout the process.  
  
The visual representation of these models takes the form of a spiral, with the beginning planning and requirements gathering step as the center point. Each loop or phase represents the entire software delivery cycle. At the start of each new phase, teams can modify requirements, review testing and adjust any code as needed. The spiral model offers risk-management benefits and is ideal for large, complex projects.

A spline camera moves along a smooth curve defined by control points. It is useful for cutscenes, introductions, and guided views where authored motion should pass through a sequence of locations without sharp corners.

Position can be evaluated from a [[Catmull-Rom Spline]], while orientation may follow a separate target or interpolated path. Timing determines how quickly the camera traverses each curve segment.

A split-complementary scheme begins with one base hue and replaces its direct complement with the two hues adjacent to that complement. It preserves noticeable contrast while distributing it across a less confrontational relationship.

The base hue can establish the environmental field while the two opposing hues separate different accents or gameplay categories. Value and saturation control keep the three colors hierarchical instead of equally dominant.

A spring follow camera treats the desired follow position as an anchor connected to the actual camera by a damped spring. Displacement creates a restoring force, while damping reduces oscillation.

The resulting lag smooths sudden target motion and can make the view feel more natural than a rigid [[Follow Camera]]. Spring constants and damping must be tuned so responsiveness is preserved without jitter or prolonged overshoot.

A Sprint Goal is the coherent outcome a team intends to achieve during a [[Sprint]]. It gives the selected backlog work a shared purpose and supports trade-offs when details change.

For a game team, a strong goal describes playable value or the reduction of an important risk. Completing unrelated discipline tasks is weaker because it postpones integration and obscures whether the player experience improved.

A Sprint is a fixed one-to-three-week interval in which a [[Scrum Team]] pursues a [[Sprint Goal]] and produces a usable [[Product Increment]]. Its stable duration creates a regular opportunity to inspect the product and adapt both plans and practices.

A Sprint contains planning, daily coordination, development, review, and retrospective work. It is not merely a deadline for a batch of disconnected tasks.

A Sprint reset ends and replans a Sprint when its goal has become obsolete or impossible. Incomplete backlog items return to the Product Backlog and the team begins planning again from the changed reality.

A reset is deliberately rare because it discards coordination and creates overhead. Ordinary discovery should be handled by adapting the Sprint plan while preserving the goal.

A Sprint Retrospective inspects how a team created value and identifies a small improvement to try in the next Sprint. A simple format asks what to stop, start, and continue, then assigns and tracks the chosen action.

The event focuses on the working system, relationships, tools, and practices. It turns [[Continuous Improvement]] into an explicit recurring responsibility.

A sprite component attaches a two-dimensional image and drawing behavior to a [[Game Actor]]. It derives its position, scale, and rotation from the actor while storing presentation-specific data such as texture, dimensions, and draw order.

The renderer maintains sprite components in sorted order so the [[2D Painter's Algorithm]] produces the intended layering. An animated specialization can change texture regions over time without altering the actor model.

A sprite is a two-dimensional image rendered as a discrete game object or visual element. Its texture, position, scale, orientation, and drawing order determine how it appears in the scene.

Animated sprites select successive source images over time, often from a [[Sprite Sheet]]. Sprites remain the primary visual building block of many 2D games even though modern displays and assets are much larger than their early counterparts.

A sprite sheet packs multiple sprite images or animation frames into one larger texture. Rendering selects a rectangular region of that texture rather than loading a separate image for every pose.

Packing reduces texture changes and keeps related frames together. [[Sprite Animation]] advances the selected region according to its own timing rather than assuming one animation image per rendered frame.

A spurious correlation is a statistical association that does not reflect the causal relationship a decision maker assumes. Variables may move together by chance, because both depend on another factor, or because the data collection process created the pattern.

Machine learning can exploit such associations successfully within training data while failing when conditions change. The ethical risk grows when correlation is used to judge a person, allocate an opportunity, or justify intervention. High predictive performance does not by itself establish that the inferred relationship is meaningful, fair, or appropriate for action.

A SQLite mobile cache stores structured application data in an embedded relational database on the device. It supports indexed queries and relationships that would be cumbersome in an unstructured key-value cache, while remaining available without a network connection.

Libraries such as SQLite.NET map .NET model attributes to tables and indexes. Local persistence does not itself synchronize with the server; the application must define which records are authoritative and how concurrent changes are resolved.

A square matrix has the same number of rows and columns, so its size is $n\times n$. Square shape permits operations and properties that rectangular matrices do not have, including a [[Determinant]], [[Matrix Trace]], eigenvalues, and possibly a [[Matrix Inverse]].

Important square-matrix families include [[Diagonal Matrix]], [[Upper Triangular Matrix]], [[Symmetric Matrix]], and [[Orthogonal Matrix]].

A square matrix is strictly diagonally dominant when, in every row, the absolute diagonal entry is greater than the sum of the absolute values of all other entries in that row.

This structural condition guarantees nonsingularity and supplies a useful sufficient condition for convergence of the [[Jacobi Method]] and [[Gauss-Seidel Method]]. It is sufficient, not necessary: some nondominant systems also converge.

A square root of (a) is a number whose [[Square]] equals (a). The radical notation (sqrt{a}) denotes the nonnegative square root when (a\geq0); for example, (sqrt{25}=5) because (5^2=25).

A positive number also has a negative value whose square is the same, which is why solving (x^2=25) gives (x=5) or (x=-5). If a natural number is not a perfect square, its square root is irrational. Negative real numbers do not have real square roots.

A stabilized approach keeps configuration, speed, power, vertical path, sink rate, and checklists within the aircraft and operator's defined limits by a specified altitude. Those conditions must then remain stable through landing. If they are not achieved or are lost, a go-around is the planned corrective action rather than an exceptional failure.

A stacked area time-series plot accumulates component series so the outer boundary represents their total. It is meaningful when the variables are additive parts of a global quantity and supports reading contribution and total change together. Only the first component has a stable baseline; internal layers are harder to compare precisely. Layer order therefore affects interpretation, and components that do not form a meaningful sum should not be stacked.

A stacked autoencoder builds a deep representation by placing several encoders in sequence. Layers may be pretrained one at a time as autoencoders before the entire stack is fine-tuned.

Successive hidden layers transform the input into increasingly abstract features. Bottlenecks, sparsity, denoising, and supervised objectives can be combined to shape the learned representation.

A stacked bar chart partitions each bar according to the levels of a second categorical variable. It shows both the size of the primary groups and how the secondary outcome is distributed within them.

The first segment has a common baseline, while later segments do not, so subtle comparisons can be difficult. Frequencies, proportions, and the intended denominator should therefore be made explicit in the labels or accompanying table.

The book uses the stacked form to display a second category within each group and contrasts it with filled and dodged variants. That comparison makes the choice of denominator and baseline an explicit design decision.

A stage gate is a deliberate checkpoint at which a project is evaluated for viability, progress, risk, and continued investment. A concept may pass forward, return for significant revision, or be removed from active development.

Stage gates bound an otherwise open-ended [[Design-Build-Test Loop]]. They allow exploration while preventing iteration from becoming indefinite motion without progress, and they preserve rejected ideas for possible future use rather than forcing sunk-cost continuation.

A gate can coexist with agile delivery when it evaluates demonstrated results, current risks, and updated forecasts. Treating the gate as approval of a frozen speculative plan instead suppresses the evidence that iteration was meant to produce.

A staging deployment installs a release candidate into a nonproduction environment before live promotion. It provides a hosted destination for checking the artifact, environment settings, network relationships, and application startup.

Passing staging supplies additional release evidence but does not erase environmental differences. The pipeline must use the correct staging configuration and define how promotion follows verification.

A staging environment is a pre-production deployment used to verify a published application under conditions closer to production than ordinary development. It creates a place to test configuration, hosting, networking, and deployment output before public release.

Staging should remain separate from production data and credentials while resembling the production topology closely enough to expose environment-specific faults.

A staging slot is a nonproduction App Service destination used to host a release candidate before promotion. The deployment pipeline can install the new artifact there and run checks against an accessible environment.

Staging provides evidence about the deployable package and hosted configuration without immediately replacing production. It is useful only when its differences from production are understood and intentional.

A stakeholder is a person or group with a meaningful interest in a product's outcome. Players, publishers, platform holders, business leaders, and dependent teams can each supply constraints, feedback, or value judgments.

Stakeholders collaborate through the [[Product Owner]] and inspect working results at the [[Sprint Review]]. Their participation grounds decisions in product evidence without turning the Development Team into a committee-controlled task pool.

A standard error is the standard deviation of a statistic's [[Sampling Distribution]]. It measures how much the estimate would vary if the data-generating and sampling process were repeated.

For a sample mean under the [[Central Limit Theorem]], the population standard deviation is divided by the square root of sample size. In practice the unknown population spread is estimated, which introduces the t-distribution in small samples.

A standing wave forms when similar waves traveling in opposite directions superpose. Fixed nodes have zero amplitude, while antinodes have maximum amplitude, and adjacent nodes are separated by half a wavelength. The pattern transfers no net energy along the medium and appears only at frequencies compatible with the boundary conditions.

A star network topology connects peripheral nodes to a central hub rather than directly to one another. Communication between peripheral devices passes through that central node.

Individual peripheral links can fail without disconnecting every other node, and the shape is straightforward to extend. The hub remains a shared dependency whose failure can interrupt the whole network.

A state transition model describes the probability of a system's current hidden state given its preceding state. It captures the dynamics that carry information forward through an iterative probabilistic model.

The model supports prediction before a new measurement is considered. Actions or controls can also condition the transition when the system's evolution depends on an intervention.

A state-space controller represents every relevant system configuration and the events that move the system between configurations. Outputs or indicators can be defined from the active state.

Unlike a probabilistic queueing model, the purpose may be to implement deterministic control logic. Explicit states and transitions make missing cases, impossible moves, and unsafe responses easier to inspect.

A stateful web application retains information from a user's earlier requests, such as an active session. If that state lives only in one server process, later requests may need sticky routing to the same instance, making horizontal scaling and failure recovery harder. A shared durable store can preserve session continuity across instances, but introduces its own availability and consistency requirements.

A stateless web application does not require the server handling a request to retain session information for the next request. Any healthy instance can process a later call when the needed context accompanies the request or resides in an appropriate shared service. This permits more even load balancing and simpler recovery after an instance fails, though the wider system may still contain durable state elsewhere.

A static evaluation function estimates the desirability of a nonterminal game state when adversarial search cannot expand the complete [[Game Tree]]. It combines measurable features into a score from the current player's perspective.

The function must be quick because search invokes it at many leaves. Its approximation shapes the decisions of depth-limited [[Minimax]], so feature weights and blind spots can matter more than searching one additional shallow branch.

A static field is shared by all instances of a type. A constant is substituted into calling code at compile time and must be expressible as a supported literal, while a readonly field is assigned at declaration or construction and remains a live field reference.

Readonly fields are safer for public values that may change between library versions because callers observe the field after recompilation of the library. Constants are appropriate only when the value is truly permanent and known at compile time.

A static small-multiple complement places selected animation frames together on one page. Animation emphasizes movement, while the static array supports simultaneous comparison of positions and relationships at known times. The source recommends using both for a space-time raster because neither fully replaces the other. Shared scales and clear time labels let the static panels serve as a durable reference for the transient sequence.

A stationarity feature measures whether a time series maintains stable statistical behavior over time. Tests and summary statistics can indicate changes in level, variance, or other distributional properties.

Stationarity matters because many temporal models assume that their governing relationships do not drift. A feature encoding departures from that assumption can distinguish series and guide the choice of forecasting or transformation methods.

A stationary point of a differentiable function is a point where its [[Gradient]] is the zero vector. It is a candidate for an extremum, but it need not be a maximum or minimum.

The local classification depends on curvature. The [[Hessian Matrix]] can identify a [[Local Minimum]], [[Local Maximum]], or [[Saddle Point]] when its definiteness is conclusive.

A stationary study solves the state in which time derivatives vanish, making it appropriate for equilibrium operating conditions. A time-dependent study advances from an initial condition and records how temperature, flow, and stored energy evolve.

The choice follows the question rather than a preference for shorter runs. A stationary model cannot report warm-up time or transient overshoot, while a time-dependent model may use a stationary solution as an efficient initial state for later changing conditions.

A statistical code module is a short file devoted to one coherent operation, such as importing data, checking distributions, recoding variables, fitting models, or producing tables. Focused modules make the purpose and output of each stage easier to inspect.

Modules should be organized into an explicit [[Reproducible Statistical Pipeline]]. When an early definition changes, the analyst can rerun the ordered stages and verify that every downstream dataset and result reflects the correction.

A statistical language model assigns probabilities to word sequences. During speech recognition, it favors hypotheses that form plausible linguistic continuations even when the acoustic signal alone is ambiguous.

The language score is combined with the [[Acoustic Model]] during [[Speech Recognition Search]]. Traditional recognizers commonly use an [[N-Gram Language Model]], while neural systems can model longer context.

A strategy game emphasizes planning, resource use, positioning, and decisions whose consequences unfold over time. The player manages forces or systems to achieve objectives against an opponent or environment.

Good strategy preserves several viable approaches and provides enough information for plans to be formed and revised. Real-time and turn-based structures change the amount of time pressure without eliminating the need for strategic choice.

A stream function is a scalar representation of two-dimensional incompressible flow whose derivatives give orthogonal velocity components. Curves of constant stream function are streamlines.

It automatically satisfies mass conservation in the plane. The choice between stream function and velocity potential depends on geometry and which boundary conditions are simpler to express.

A streamgraph represents additive time-series components as flowing colored bands arranged around a varying baseline. Like a [[ThemeRiver]], it emphasizes changes in composition and the overall shape of the total. The organic layout can make emergence and decline easy to notice, but position changes and curved boundaries impede precise comparison. It should therefore use a restrained qualitative palette and provide labels or interaction when individual components must be identified.

A streaming feature setting presents new dimensions sequentially for a collection of observations. The learner must decide how to use or retain each feature without knowing the complete feature space in advance.

This differs from an ordinary data stream because variables, rather than cases, are the arriving objects. Irreversible decisions, feature order, redundancy, and the cost of storing accepted dimensions shape the algorithm.

A streaming instance setting presents new observations over time while the set of measured variables is comparatively stable. Feature extractors update their state from each instance rather than repeatedly processing the complete history.

Online dimension reduction and latent-variable methods operate in this regime. Their challenge is to approximate batch representations with limited memory while remaining responsive to changes in the data distribution.

A streaming recommender system updates or produces recommendations from interactions that arrive continuously. It must respond to changing interests and new items without rebuilding the entire model after every event.

Streaming design balances freshness against computation and stability. Online updates, bounded state, and time-sensitive evaluation become important when the usefulness of a preference signal decays quickly.

A streamline is a curve whose tangent at every point aligns with the instantaneous local velocity vector. In steady flow, the streamline pattern does not change with time and traces particle trajectories.

Stream functions label streamlines by constant values in two-dimensional incompressible flow. Around an impermeable body, the surface itself becomes a streamline because normal velocity is zero.

A streamline map draws curves that are tangent to a [[Vector Field Map]] at each point. The curves reveal continuous flow structure, convergence, and circulation more readily than isolated arrows. Their spacing and seeds are graphical choices rather than measurements, and a streamline does not necessarily trace the path of a physical particle through a changing field. Direction cues and a magnitude encoding may be added when shape alone is insufficient.

A stress concentration factor is the ratio of maximum local stress to a nominal reference stress. Holes and other geometric discontinuities raise local stress above the value predicted from net or gross section averages.

Analytical factors offer a benchmark for finite element results. Accurate numerical estimation requires a mesh fine enough around the discontinuity to resolve the steep gradient.

A stress-strain curve plots force per unit area against fractional deformation. Its initial linear gradient is [[Young's Modulus]]. The end of proportional behavior, elastic limit, yield region, ultimate tensile stress, and fracture point distinguish stiffness, recoverability, strength, and ductility. The curve describes material behavior independently of the specimen's original dimensions.

A string is a finite sequence of symbols from an [[Alphabet]]. Its length counts symbols, concatenation appends one sequence to another, and reversal lists the same symbols in the opposite order.

String equality requires both equal length and the same symbol in every position. Concatenation is associative but generally not commutative, and the [[Empty String]] serves as its identity.

A string text representation treats a document as an encoded sequence of characters. Byte sequences interpreted through standards such as UTF-8 can represent written symbols from many languages without first assuming words, grammar, or meaning.

This shallow form supports operations such as approximate matching, spelling correction, plagiarism alignment, and spam similarity. It is general but poorly suited to semantic tasks because character sequence alone does not expose word identity or higher linguistic structure.

A strip represents a piece of media or an effect on the Sequencer timeline. It can be added from Blender's file browser, dragged from the operating system, or created through the Add menu.

Sidebar controls set a strip's name, start frame, channel, blend behavior, crop, timing, lock, and mute state. Higher channels can overlap lower ones, giving the sequence both temporal order and a visual stack.

A structural damping matrix represents mechanisms that dissipate vibrational energy and oppose motion. It contributes a force proportional to nodal velocity in the standard linear dynamic equation.

The primer identifies damping as an additional matrix needed beyond stiffness and mass for general vibration analysis. Its presence limits resonance and governs decay in transient motion.

A structural mass matrix distributes element mass among nodal degrees of freedom so inertia can enter the finite element equations. Its coefficients depend on density, geometry, element length, and interpolation functions.

Element mass matrices are assembled using the same local-to-global mapping as stiffness matrices. In free vibration, the global mass matrix is multiplied by squared frequency in the generalized eigenvalue problem.

A structural text representation describes syntactic or semantic relationships among words, phrases, and sentences. Parse-derived constructions can capture sentence organization that a [[Bag-of-Words Representation]] discards.

These features are useful when style, grammatical competence, authorship, or semantic roles matter. Their greater linguistic depth usually brings language dependence, parsing error, and computational cost, so shallow representations may remain preferable for robust topic-oriented tasks.

A Sturm sequence is a recurrence of polynomials used to count how many eigenvalues of a symmetric tridiagonal matrix lie below a chosen value.

Comparing sign variations brackets eigenvalues and supports interval refinement. It locates individual eigenvalues without first forming all roots of a [[Characteristic Polynomial]].

A subgroup is a subset of a group that is itself a group under the restricted operation. It shares the ambient identity and the inverse of each of its elements.

Subgroups capture internal symmetry and supply the pieces used to form cosets and quotient groups.

A submodule N of an R-module M is a subset closed under addition and multiplication by scalars from R. Equivalently, it contains every R-linear combination of its elements.

An [[Ideal]] is precisely a submodule of a ring viewed as a module over itself. A submodule can be divided out to form a [[Quotient Module]] and can appear as the kernel or image in an exact sequence.

A succinct constraint lets eligible items be selected directly before candidate generation. Conditions such as an item's category or value belonging to a specified range can reduce the transaction representation and the pattern search space immediately.

This property is valuable in distributed mining because it avoids communicating and processing items that cannot appear in a valid result.

A summary statistic reduces a distribution to a numerical feature such as its count, mean, standard deviation, median, range, skewness, or standard error. Different measures describe different aspects of center, spread, and shape.

No single statistic fully describes a variable. Means and standard deviations can be misleading for strongly skewed data, so they should be read alongside [[Quantile|quantiles]] and visualizations such as histograms or box plots.
